Topic modeling (LDA) of abstracts

Source: R/topics.R
topic_model.Rd

Fits a Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic model to the abstracts in a data frame, such as the one returned by [bib_to_df()]. Each abstract is treated as a mixture of `k` topics and each topic as a distribution over words. Fitting uses a collapsed Gibbs sampler written in C++.

Usage

topic_model(
  data,
  k = 5,
  text = "abstract",
  id = "bibkey",
  n_iter = 1000,
  alpha = 5/k,
  beta = 0.01,
  min_doc_freq = 2,
  max_doc_prop = 1,
  min_word_length = 3,
  stopwords = NULL,
  singularize = TRUE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per reference.

k

Number of topics (at least 2).

text

Name of the column holding the text to analyse.

id

Name of a column that identifies each reference (default `"bibkey"`). If it does not exist, row numbers are used.

n_iter

Number of Gibbs sampling sweeps.

alpha

Prior on how many topics each abstract mixes. Smaller values mean each abstract concentrates on fewer topics. Default `5 / k`.

beta

Prior on how many words each topic uses. Smaller values mean more focused topics.

min_doc_freq

Drop words that occur in fewer than this many abstracts.

max_doc_prop

Drop words that occur in more than this share of the abstracts (1 keeps everything; try 0.5 to remove words common to nearly every abstract).

min_word_length

Drop words shorter than this many letters.

stopwords

Extra words to drop, in addition to [citelens_stopwords()].

singularize

Merge simple plurals (default `TRUE`).

seed

Optional number passed to [set.seed()] so the fit can be reproduced.

Value

An object of class `citelens_topics`. Use [topic_terms()], [topic_documents()], [topic_summary()], [plot_topic_terms()] and [plot_topic_prevalence()] to explore it. Topics are numbered from the most to the least prevalent.

Details

Text is lower-cased, punctuation and numbers are removed, stop words (see [citelens_stopwords()]) and very short words are dropped, and simple plurals are merged (students and student count as one word). Words that occur in fewer than `min_doc_freq` abstracts are ignored.

Topic models need a reasonably large collection (dozens of abstracts or more) to give stable themes. With a handful of abstracts the output is only exploratory. Different `seed` values can give somewhat different topics; use [topic_k_search()] to help choose `k`.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata", "sample_abstracts.bib", package = "citelens")
refs <- bib_to_df(f)
filler <- c("note", "time", "follow", "shape", "touch", "studied", "evidence",
            "work", "attention", "discussion")   # words from the synthetic sample
m <- topic_model(refs, k = 3, stopwords = filler, seed = 1)
m
#> <citelens topic model>
#> 3 topics from 30 abstracts (51 distinct words, 496 word occurrences)
#> alpha = 1.67, beta = 0.01, sweeps = 1000
#> 
#>  topic prevalence n_docs coherence
#>      1        36%     10     -25.5
#>      2        33%     10     -27.2
#>      3        32%     10     -22.2
#>                                                                 top_terms
#>                               college, cost, financial, aid, budget, debt
#>  predictive, reporting, analytics, institutional, benchmarking, dashboard
#>               retention, support, advising, attrition, dropout, mentoring
topic_terms(m, n = 5)
#>    topic rank          term       beta
#> 1      1    1       college 0.07676292
#> 2      1    2          cost 0.07676292
#> 3      1    3     financial 0.07676292
#> 4      1    4           aid 0.07128377
#> 5      1    5        budget 0.07128377
#> 6      2    1    predictive 0.10036988
#> 7      2    2     reporting 0.10036988
#> 8      2    3     analytics 0.07529309
#> 9      2    4 institutional 0.07529309
#> 10     2    5  benchmarking 0.06902389
#> 11     3    1     retention 0.09652112
#> 12     3    2       support 0.09652112
#> 13     3    3      advising 0.08366021
#> 14     3    4     attrition 0.07722976
#> 15     3    5       dropout 0.07722976
